Hypothesis G: The object only moves when the click is on the r tip of the object, and the direction is toward the click? I clicked the r tip (37,16) — nothing happened.

Wait a moment — maybe in level 2, the object only moves when the click is on the g border of the container? Or maybe the container's ring is the "button," and the direction is determined by which ring (left ring → left, right ring → right)? I clicked the O left ring at (56,6) and (57,6). Nothing happened.
Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe in level 2, the piece is controlled by clicking the piece's r tip, and it moves toward the click position? I clicked (37,16), which is the tip itself. Let me try clicking the r tip and then... no, that's not it.
Let me look at the image again. Piece:
```

row37: ...YNNr.... (13,Y? no: (13,'Y')? The scan says (13,'Y')? row 37: (13,'Y'),(14,'N'),(15,'N'),(16,'r')
row38: ...SSS..... (13,S),(14,S),(15,S)

row40: ..OOO...... (10,O),(11,O),(12,O)

```

The r tip is at (37,16) — the right side of the top row.
Level 1 bar: G anchor at one end, colored body, r tip at the other end. The bar moved via the container pad.
Level 2 piece: the staircase has no G anchor... no wait, there's a G at (36,12). And the r tip is at (37,16).
Maybe the piece moves as a whole (all blocks shift) when you click the container, and the direction is determined by the click position within the container. The O container clicks did nothing...
Unless the piece can't move left/down because of a wall? No, there are no walls.
